full_judgment:
in the interest of Sree Ram Sarker under C.S.  Khatian No. 110. Sree Ram Sarker was succeeded by his two sons namely, Naddan Mistry and Narayan Mistry and the S. A. Khatian was recorded and published in their names. Upon a mutual partition among the brothers, Narayan Mistry got the right, title and possession of the suit land who has transferred the same to the proforma defendant No. 2 on 30.3.1979 under the registered deeds No. 5468 and 7243 respectively. The said proforma Defendant No. 2 has, after purchase, mutated her name and paid rent under separate Jama and on 21.5.1979 transferred the same to the plaintiff by executing a registered sale deed. But the defendant No. 1 threatened the plaintiff of dispossession from the suit land on 28.12.1979 who has no right, title and possession in the suit land and as such, the plaintiff has been obliged to institute the instant suit. 

 10. Perused the application, heard the learned Advocates and examined the judgments of the Courts below together with the evidence and materials on record. It appears that the learned trial court has relied upon the evidence of P. W. 1 as well as D. W. 1 and 2 in respect of possession holding that the D. W. I and 2 have also admitted possession of the plaintiff. The learned trial Judge has also relied upon the mutation khatian and the separate Jama to consider the evidence of the P. W. 1 that the land in question had an amicable family partition and also construed that the separation of khatian amounts to partition and thus, passed the decree. The learned Appellate Court, on the other hand, held that in the plaint of the suit the plaintiff did not state any particulars of the alleged family partition and that from the evidence on record, it has not been proved that the defendant No. 1 is not possessing any land in the disputed plots and that the plaintiff also failed to prove her title. 

 12. It appears that while the learned trial court held that the plaintiff-is in possession of the suit land, the learned Appellate Court held that the defendant No. I also cannot be said to be out of possession in the disputed plots. It further appears that the entire khatian i.e. the property of Ram Chandra Sarker and his two sons are not in dispute and it has also not been decided whether the parties are overlapping each-other. But apparently, the learned Appellate Court has not taken into consideration the mutation khatian and the separate jama which prima facie shows separate possession of the plaintiff in respect of the disputed land. The learned Appellate Court attempted to decide the title of the parties, which is not the fact in issue in the instant suit. 

 13. The learned Advocate, appearing for the opposite party pointed out the fact of not having the boundary of the disputed land in the plaint and submits that the learned Appellate Court has rightly found that the decree for permanent injunction cannot be passed where the boundary of disputed land has not specifically been stated in the plaint. Mr. S. N. Goswami, on the other hand, submits with reference to the exhibit 5 series and exhibit 6, which are rent receipts and mutation khatian in the name of the plaintiff—petitioner that these 2 exhibits have categorically identified the scheduled land of the plaintiff in respect of which she prayed for a decree for permanent injunction and as such the learned Appellate Court has taken an erroneous view in this respect. On perusal of exhibit-6 i.e. the mutation khatian and the exhibit-5 series i.e. the rent receipts in the name of the plaintiff–Petitioner, it appears that the disputed land has specifically and sufficiently identified, which is the basic purpose of mentioning the boundary in the plaint.
